heroes.name: Cyrus II
heroes.infro: Cyrus, II was the first Zoroastrian Persian Emperor.  He ruled from 576-530 B.C. and was also known as Cyrus the Great or Cyrus the Elder.  Cyrus, II founded the Persian Empire under the Achaemenid dynasty and under his 30 year reign, it expanded vastly, conquering most of Southwest Asia and much of Central Asia.  From Egypt and the Hellespont in the west to the Indus River in the east, Cyrus, II created the largest empire the world had yet seen.  He met his fate in a fierce battle with the Massagetae, a tribe from the deserts of Kharesm and Kizilhoum in the southernmost steppe regions of modern-day Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

heroes.name: Gao Guiying
heroes.infro: Gao Guiying was one of the most remarkable women in the history of China. She was a revolutionary, rebellion-leader, and served as a commander in the army training and leading female troops of rebels. As a commander of both male and female warriors, she captured Beijing, deposed the Ming dynasty and took control as regent.

heroes.name: Saladin
heroes.infro: A Muslim warrior and eventual Sultan of both Egypt and Syria, Saladin led vast armies in campaigns against European forces during the First Crusade.  Instead of being despised in Europe, many great leaders admired his chivalrous values.

heroes.name: Vasco Nunez de Balboa
heroes.infro: Balboa emigrated from Spain to Hispaniola in 1501, and, after failing as a plantation owner, he led expeditions through Central and South America. He founded the town of Darien, Panama, and--lured by gold--crossed the Peruvian Andes and discovered the Pacific Ocean in 1513. He claimed possession of the Pacific for Ferdinand II of Spain who rewarded the conquistador by making him an Admiral and Governor of Panama.

heroes.name: Beowulf
heroes.infro: Beowulf's sword, shield and bravery are a welcomed addition to any army.  A hero from Geatland, Beowulf has slain even the most formidable foes, often times without weapons just to prove his might.

heroes.name: Pachacuti
heroes.infro: The Ninth Sapa Inca, aka 'the Napoleon of the Andes'  Pachacuti began the expansion of the Inca that stretched the Empire across most of western South America.   In addition to conquering much land, he also structured the government, dividing the empire into four large territories.  To prevent any official from exerting too much influence, he created a separate bureaucracy for government administration, military command, and the priesthood.

heroes.name: Genghis Khan
heroes.infro: Famous for both his sheer lust for conquest and ability as a military tactician, Khan united small tribes in central Asia to create one of the largest empires ever known.

heroes.name: Henry IV
heroes.infro: Henry IV was king of Germany from 1056  and then Holy Roman Emperor from 1084 until 1105 when he was forced to abdicate. He was a powerful figure in the 11th century whose reign was marked by several civil wars in Italy and Germany and by the Investiture Controversy with the Pope. While gathering an army to fight his son Henry V he fell ill and died.

heroes.name: Arêtes III, King of the Nabata
heroes.infro: Arêtes III was king of the Nabataean kingdom from 87BCE to 62BCE.  He became king when his father, who was the previous king, passed away.  Arêtes III most impressive accomplishment during his reign as king is the amount of territory he brought under his rule.  In fact, Nabataea experienced its most significant territorial expansion during the kingship of Arêtes III.  Famous for his conquest of Damascus, Arêtes III held control of this powerful trade hub for several years before losing control to the Armenians.  He later retook the city with the assistance of Rome.
